task.description:
REWORK ITERATION 3 (design-level, from REVIEWER's Step 2d OQ-5 FAIL, not SECURITY-REVIEWER this time -- handoffs/WF02-REQ025-20260817/step-02d-reviewer.json): the design doc (lib/letflow/design/req025-event-append.md) has been reworked and re-validated (CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR PASS, step-01b handoff) to make M1/M6's create-vs-update contract update-only. Your job is to bring lib/letflow/event_store.ex into line with the now-current design -- the code still implements the OLD contract REVIEWER rejected. Two concrete changes required:

(1) M1 (active_instance_guard/3, ~event_store.ex:315-327): currently `nil -> {:ok, :new_instance}` when no instance_projections row exists. Per the revised design §6.2.1, this must instead fail the step: `nil -> {:error, :instance_not_started}`. The terminal-instance branch is unchanged. Since M6 will need the *existing* InstanceProjection struct (not just an atom) to build its update changeset while preserving the current status unchanged, consider having the non-terminal success branch return `{:ok, projection}` (the actual %InstanceProjection{} struct) instead of `{:ok, :existing_instance}`, so `update_projection/3` (M6) can read it back via `changes.active_instance_guard` -- this is an implementation choice, not dictated by the design doc (which deliberately specifies behavior, not Elixir data shapes), but it's the natural way to satisfy InstanceProjection.update_changeset/2's `validate_required([:status, :last_event_seq])` without a second DB read.

(2) M6 (update_projection/3, ~event_store.ex:492-512): currently builds an `%InstanceProjection{} |> InstanceProjection.insert_changeset(attrs) |> repo.insert(..., on_conflict: [...], conflict_target: :instance_id)` upsert that can create a fresh row. Per the revised design §6.2.6, replace this with a plain update: fetch the existing projection struct from M1's result (`changes.active_instance_guard`, per point 1 above, or however you choose to thread it through), call `InstanceProjection.update_changeset/2` with `%{status: existing.status, last_event_seq: assigned_sequence_number}` (status passed through unchanged -- update_changeset/2 requires it present but the design explicitly forbids M6 from changing it), and `repo.update/2` with `prefix: schema_name`. No `insert_changeset/2`, no `on_conflict:`, no `conflict_target:` anywhere in M6 after this change.

Also: append/2's `@type append_error()` (design §5.3) needs `{:error, :instance_not_started}` added as a distinct case if not already present as a literal atom your code can return (check `interpret_transaction_result/1`'s catch-all clause at the bottom of the file already passes through `{:error, reason}` for any unrecognized failed-operation reason -- confirm `:instance_not_started` flows through that catch-all correctly, or add an explicit clause if you'd rather be explicit than rely on the catch-all). Update the module's own inline comments at M1/M6 (currently describe the old create-if-absent/upsert behavior) to match the new behavior -- stale comments describing removed logic are exactly the kind of drift REVIEWER checks for.

After the code change: mix compile --warnings-as-errors, mix format --check-formatted, mix test (existing event_store tests will very likely now fail since they relied on append/2 originating a new instance's projection row on first append -- TEST-DESIGNER hasn't yet reworked test fixtures to pre-seed instance_projections per the design's new §11 note, so failures here are EXPECTED and not this step's fault; note which tests fail and why in your handoff rather than trying to fix TEST-DESIGNER's fixtures yourself, that's out of your role's scope -- TEST-DESIGNER reworks fixtures at Step 3 after this implementation passes SECURITY-REVIEWER/REVIEWER again). Do not touch anything else in the file -- M2-M5, the pre-transaction phase P0-P6, and tenant_provisioning.ex's tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 all passed both SECURITY-REVIEWER and REVIEWER already and are out of scope for this rework.

ORIGINAL REWORK ITERATION 2 (kept for history, already resolved -- do not re-touch): SECURITY-REVIEWER re-validated and FAILed again on INV-8, same invariant, narrower gap (handoffs/WF02-REQ025-20260817/step-02c-security-reviewer.json, second FAIL). Your iteration-1 fix added `when not is_map(metadata)` as validate_metadata/1's leading guard -- but a struct IS a map in Elixir (is_map/1 returns true for structs), so it doesn't exclude them. SECURITY-REVIEWER confirmed real crashes: DateTime.utc_now() and URI.parse(...) raise Protocol.UndefinedError (no Enumerable impl); MapSet.new([1,2,3]) and 1..5 (a Range struct) raise FunctionClauseError inside validate_metadata/1's own `fn {key, value} -> ... end` since structs iterate as bare elements via Enum, not {key, value} tuples. Fix: change the guard to also reject structs, e.g. `when not is_map(metadata) or is_struct(metadata)` (a struct is never a valid metadata value here -- only a plain, non-struct map is). After fixing, do a wider sweep yourself of every place in the pre-transaction phase (P0-P6) that calls Enum.*/Map.*/String.* on caller-supplied input without first ruling out structs specifically (is_map/1 alone is not sufficient anywhere in this codebase's pattern, since every struct also satisfies it) -- check idempotency_key, payload, event_type, and any other attrs field the same way, not just metadata again. REWORK ITERATION 1: SECURITY-REVIEWER FAILed on INV-8 (handoffs/WF02-REQ025-20260817/step-02c-security-reviewer.json). validate_metadata/1 in lib/letflow/event_store.ex (~line 233) RAISES instead of returning a typed {:error, _} on realistic malformed attrs[:metadata] input: an empty string or integer raises Protocol.UndefinedError; a non-tuple list or an atom-keyed map (e.g. %{foo: "bar"} -- an easy mistake since every other attrs key in this module is an atom) raises FunctionClauseError inside String.length/1. append/2's own @spec promises {:ok, _} | {:error, _} -- a raised exception on caller-controlled input violates that contract. Fix validate_metadata/1 (and audit the rest of the pre-transaction validation phase, P0-P6, for the same class of bug -- guard on is_map/1, is_binary/1, is_list/1 etc. before calling functions like String.length/1/Enum.count/1 that assume a specific shape) so every realistic malformed-attrs shape returns a typed {:error, {:invalid_metadata, _}}-shaped tuple (or whatever the design's error taxonomy already names) rather than raising. Add a regression check yourself (throwaway iex/mix run, not part of your committed artifacts) confirming at least: metadata as a non-map, metadata as an atom-keyed map, and metadata as a string, all now return {:error, _} rather than raising. Implement lib/letflow/design/req025-event-append.md's design: a new lib/letflow/event_store.ex context module (Letflow.EventStore) with append/2, per the design's Section 6 algorithm (now prose, not code -- your job is to turn that prose into real, correct Elixir/Ecto). Also add Letflow.TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 (the reverse of schema_name_for_tenant/1) to lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex, per the design's Section 4. No new migrations needed -- REQ-023 already created every table this touches. The design's OQ-5 (instance_projections insert-if-absent at first append) needs REVIEWER's explicit confirmation at Step 2d -- implement per the design's stated resolution but flag it again in your own handoff so it isn't missed.
acceptance_criteria: appending to a terminated instance (status CANCELLED or COMPLETED in instance_projections) returns an error and writes zero rows across all five involved tables, demonstrated by an actual test or iex session against a real Postgres, not just described

two concurrent appends to the same instance_id never receive the same sequence_number -- demonstrated with an actual concurrent test (e.g. Task.async_stream racing two appends) or, if concurrency can't be exercised in this environment, the FOR UPDATE-equivalent locking code path is cited explicitly
appending twice with the same idempotency_key returns is_duplicate: true on the second call and does not insert a second events row, verified against the idempotency sidecar table REQ-023 defines
a payload that fails REQ-024's validate_payload/2 results in zero rows written to events, instance_sequence, or instance_projections -- no partial state
a payload over 4096 bytes is split into events.payload's $ref pointer form plus an event_payload_store row, verified by reading both rows back after append

every row append/1(2) writes (events, instance_sequence, instance_projections, the idempotency sidecar) has tenant_id equal to the tenant whose schema the write targeted, derived internally -- not equal to a caller-supplied tenant_id when the two are deliberately made to disagree in a test, which must fail loudly (not silently attribute to the wrong tenant) rather than succeed

result.summary:
REWORK ITERATION 3 -- brought lib/letflow/event_store.ex into line with the design doc's already-reworked, already-re-validated (CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR PASS) update-only contract for M1/M6, resolving REVIEWER's Step 2d OQ-5 FAIL (step-02d-reviewer.json). Read the design doc's current §6.2.1 and §6.2.6 directly before changing code, not from the handoff summary alone.

Change 1 -- M1 (active_instance_guard/3, event_store.ex): the no-row branch previously succeeded with `{:ok, :new_instance}`; now fails the Multi step with `{:error, :instance_not_started}`, per design §6.2.1. The terminal-instance branch (`{:error, {:instance_terminated, status}}`) is unchanged. The non-terminal success branch now returns `{:ok, projection}` -- the actual `%InstanceProjection{}` struct, not the bare `:existing_instance` atom it returned before -- so M6 can read the row's current `status` back via `changes.active_instance_guard` without a second DB read.

Change 2 -- M6 (update_projection/3, event_store.ex): replaced the `%InstanceProjection{} |> InstanceProjection.insert_changeset(attrs) |> repo.insert(prefix: ..., on_conflict: [...], conflict_target: :instance_id)` upsert with a plain update: the function now pattern-matches `active_instance_guard: %InstanceProjection{} = projection` out of `changes` (M1's result), builds `attrs = %{status: projection.status, last_event_seq: assigned_sequence_number}` (status passed through unchanged -- required by `update_changeset/2`'s `validate_required([:status, :last_event_seq])` but never actually changed by an ordinary append), and calls `projection |> InstanceProjection.update_changeset(attrs) |> repo.update(prefix: schema_name)`. No `insert_changeset/2`, no `on_conflict:`, no `conflict_target:` remain anywhere in M6.

Type/error-flow check: added `{:error, :instance_not_started}` as an explicit case in `@type append_error()` (it was previously only reachable through the generic `{:error, term()}` catch-all type, which is structurally sound but not the pattern-matchable named tag the design doc's §5.3 specifies). Traced `interpret_transaction_result/1`: `{:error, :active_instance_guard, :instance_not_started, _changes}` has no dedicated clause and falls through to the existing generic `{:error, _failed_operation, reason, _changes} -> {:error, reason}` catch-all at the bottom of the file, which re-surfaces it correctly as `{:error, :instance_not_started}` -- confirmed by reading the clause, not assumed; added an explanatory comment above that catch-all rather than a redundant dedicated clause, since the existing one already handles it correctly.

Stale comments updated: M1's inline comment (previously silent on the old `{:ok, :new_instance}` behavior, now explicitly documents the update-only contract and why the struct is threaded through). M6's inline comment (previously described "a genuine insert-if-absent-else-update, expressed as one atomic on_conflict statement" -- now describes the plain update and cites the M1 guarantee it relies on). Also updated the module's own moduledoc "Scope" paragraph, which still read "`append/2` only ever creates or advances the bare row" -- changed to state append/2 never originates the row and fails with `{:error, :instance_not_started}` when one doesn't exist, citing REVIEWER's Step 2d OQ-5 ruling explicitly.

Out of scope, confirmed untouched: M2 (assign_sequence -- instance_sequence's own insert-if-absent via on_conflict:, a structurally different table/step, correctly left alone), M3 (claim_idempotency), M4 (insert_event), M5 (store_oversized_payload), the entire pre-transaction phase P0-P6, and tenant_provisioning.ex. Grepped the whole file afterward for `on_conflict`/`insert-if-absent`/`instance_projections` to confirm no other stale reference to the old M6 upsert behavior remains -- the only remaining `on_conflict:`/`conflict_target:` occurrences are M2's and M3's, both out of scope and unchanged.

Verification actually run (not predicted): `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` -- exits 0, output `Compiling 1 file (.ex)` / `Generated letflow app`, no warnings. `mix format --check-formatted` -- exits 0, no output (nothing unformatted). `mix test` (real docker-compose Postgres on port 5462, confirmed `Up 4 hours (healthy)` via `docker compose ps` before running) -- `4 properties, 401 tests, 0 failures`. Note on the task's expectation that event_store tests would 'very likely now fail': there is currently no `test/letflow/event_store_test.exs` file in the repo at all (confirmed via `find . -iname event_store_test.exs`, no match; `test/letflow/event_store/` only contains `migrations_test.exs`, `registry_test.exs`, `schemas_test.exs`, and a `registry/` subdirectory) -- TEST-DESIGNER has not yet written append/2's test suite, so there was nothing to fail. This is consistent with the task's own framing (TEST-DESIGNER reworks/writes fixtures at Step 3, after this implementation passes SECURITY-REVIEWER/REVIEWER again) -- 401/401 passing is the full existing suite (event_type_registry, tenant_provisioning, schema modules, etc.), unrelated to this change, still green.
issues: No event_store_test.exs exists yet for append/2 -- flagging explicitly (not silently discovered by TEST-DESIGNER later) so Step 3's TEST-DESIGNER knows this is a from-scratch test suite, not a rework of an existing one, and must pre-seed instance_projections rows via direct Repo.insert per the design doc's §11 acceptance-criteria-traceability note (REVIEWER-confirmed test strategy) before exercising append/2 in any AC1-AC6 test.

OQ-1 (design doc §9, carried over unchanged, out of this step's scope to resolve): instance_sequence and event_idempotency carry no tenant_id column; TEST-DESIGNER must adapt AC6's test to a prefix-reachability check for those two tables rather than a column-value check, per the design doc's own stated resolution.

OQ-4/OQ-6 (design doc §9, carried over unchanged, out of this step's scope): OQ-4 (event_type has no standalone error atom, surfaces via Ecto.Changeset instead) and OQ-6 (M1's active-instance guard is an unlocked read) remain open per the design doc; neither was touched by this rework iteration since both are pre-transaction-phase/M1-read-semantics questions the design doc did not change in its OQ-5 rework.
